$comment: Hand-maintained. Declares the LAYERED governance packages that control this repository, how their integrity is verified, and — since AWE-0 — how each accepted architecture package is bound to the repository's ADR, module-state and Horizon authority. Verified in CI by scripts/check-network-governance.mjs (integrity) and scripts/check-architecture-governance.mjs (binding). This file exists separately from handoff-provenance.json on purpose: that file is regenerated wholesale by scripts/sync-handoff.mjs, which rebuilds its object from HANDOFF_VERSION/HANDOFF_SOURCE and preserves only `overrides`, so any layer declaration added there would be silently dropped on the next `pnpm sync:handoff`. Overloading its single handoffVersion string to mean three packages would also make the base-layer provenance check ambiguous.
subordination: Network architecture is ADDITIVE and SUBORDINATE to the production handoff and to the security, privacy, tenant-isolation, authority, resilience and non-regression requirements that precede it. Where a network requirement and a security requirement conflict, the stricter restriction wins and the network requirement yields. No layer below may be weakened to simplify a layer above.

architectureGovernance.$comment: AWE-0. Closes W01-F-GOV-01 and the root defect recorded in docs/agentic-architecture-review/01_PACKAGE_INVENTORY_AND_PRECEDENCE.md §3.1-§3.2: six accepted architecture packages (607 files) were substantive and internally coherent while being declared nowhere, verified by nothing, and connected to no accepted ADR in either direction. Registration binds a package to authority. It NEVER confers any.
authorizationLadder: ARCHITECTURE EXISTS — files are on disk under docs/production-handoff/.
ARCHITECTURE IS ACCEPTED — the package is declared here with governanceStatus=accepted and its manifest verifies.
IMPLEMENTATION IS AUTHORIZED — config/scope/module_states.yaml puts the module in an implementable state at or below horizon_authorized. A package declaration cannot reach this rung.
CAPABILITY IS IMPLEMENTED — code, migrations and tests exist and pass.
CAPABILITY IS CERTIFIED/LIVE — the applicable acceptance gate is signed and the module is activated.
architectureGovernance.runtimeAuthorityRule: No runtime gate may read this file. Registering a documentation package must never make a runtime check pass. scripts/check-architecture-governance.mjs asserts that no file under packages/*/src/ references governance-layers.json, so the separation is structural rather than promised.
architectureGovernance.precedenceRule: `precedence` orders the governance LAYERS only, lowest number first. It is a tie-break for two texts that both apply, not a licence: regardless of precedence the stricter accepted restriction wins, and security, tenant-isolation, authority, privacy, legal, resilience and certification constraints fail closed. An additive-subordinate layer may never carry a lower precedence number than a base or controlling layer.
authorityAboveArchitecture: adr/ — accepted repository ADRs, enforced in code
config/scope/module_states.yaml — machine-readable module and Horizon authority, enforced by scripts/validate-scope.mjs

adrRelationVocabulary.governed-by: The ADR rules the matter. Where the package and the ADR differ, the ADR wins.
adrRelationVocabulary.constrained-by: The ADR bounds the package without deciding its content.
adrRelationVocabulary.additive-beneath: The package adds detail under the ADR and does not touch its decision.

architectureGovernance.unresolvedAuthorityRule: An architecture claim with no accepted ADR behind it belongs in `unresolvedAuthority`, which may not name an ADR. Registering a package does not resolve anything it leaves open; the entries below stay visible until an owner decision or a later package closes them.

layers.note: The base handoff. Its integrity is verified in CI by `sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS.txt`, and its generated operational copies at the repository root are verified by scripts/check-handoff-provenance.mjs. handoff-provenance.json describes THIS layer only.
Controlling security layer. Generates no root copies. Its manifest was unverified by CI before N0 — the same gap the audit found in v1.4.0, and it is closed by the same validator.

Network architecture. Additive and subordinate. Installing it authorizes no runtime behavior: no participants, integrations, agents, dispatch, marketplace or settlement activate because a document describes them. Carries no `architecture` block: its ADR authority is the accepted docs/decisions/ N-series recorded during N0-N7, not AWE-0.

Enterprise agent operations. Self-declared: "additive to all existing FreightOS production handoffs, especially v1.3.0 Security/Privacy/Resilience and v1.4.0 Network Architecture. It does not replace or weaken any existing accepted requirement." moduleScope is the reviewed registration act this file exists to hold; the package itself names no module id from config/scope/module_states.yaml.

adrRelations.evidence: ADR-0013 authorizes Horizon 1 production implementation only and preserves the rest of the ecosystem as contracts, schemas, disabled configuration, fixtures and simulation. It is the decision that lets this package be complete design while remaining unimplementable.
ADR-0014 fixes the handoff location and the immutability of an installed package. This package lives under docs/production-handoff/ and is byte-pinned by its MANIFEST.json.
ADR-0004 requires agents to act through typed commands. An enterprise agent-operations design may not introduce an action path that bypasses the command boundary.
ADR-0018 computes the autonomy ceiling from module state rather than trusting a declared value; scripts/validate-scope.mjs clamps every agent to it. No agent-operations design raises that ceiling.

unresolvedAuthority.note: docs/agentic-architecture-review/06_ACTION_COMMAND_POLICY_VOCABULARY_AUDIT.md finds two disjoint command vocabularies across the corpus and no accepted registry either side must conform to. AWE-2 is the named remedy; AWE-0 records the gap rather than closing it.

ADR-0025 supplies the policy-driven detention mechanism, the required policy-field table and scope precedence. docs/agentic-architecture-review/01_PACKAGE_INVENTORY_AND_PRECEDENCE.md §3.2 records that FacilityOS 11_APPOINTMENTS_CAPACITY_AND_DETENTION.md:40-57 still leaves all of it open, so the repository is ahead of the package here and ADR-0025 governs.
